subject: Pharmacology
concept: Therapy for toxoplasmosis and human African trypanosomiasis is selected according to disease stage, severity and host factors.

content.definition: Antiparasitic treatment varies with organism, stage and immune status.
content.explanation: Serious toxoplasmosis commonly uses a pyrimethamine-based combination with a sulfonamide and folinic acid in appropriate patients; human African trypanosomiasis therapy differs by parasite species and CNS involvement.
content.mechanism: Toxoplasmosis regimens inhibit parasite folate metabolism; trypanosomiasis drugs have stage- and species-specific antiparasitic mechanisms.
content.clinical_relevance: CNS disease is a major determinant of treatment selection in African trypanosomiasis, while immune status strongly influences toxoplasmosis management.
content.treatment: Treatment should follow current specialist and public-health guidance for the specific species, stage and host.
high_yield: Toxoplasmosis therapy depends on clinical form and immune status.
Folinic acid is used with pyrimethamine-based therapy to reduce host folate toxicity.
Trypanosomiasis treatment differs between T. brucei gambiense and T. brucei rhodesiense and by CNS stage.
Drug toxicity and monitoring requirements are regimen-specific.

yemen_context.relevance: Included in the official Hematology Pharmacology syllabus as antiparasitic therapy.
yemen_context.evidence: General evidence; no Yemen-specific regimen asserted.

review_notes: Original educational synthesis using WHO/CDC and clinical reference principles.
